title: Should cars be banned from the city centre?
instructions: You are going to listen to a radio discussion about a plan to ban private cars from a city centre. For questions 1–8, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which fits best according to what you hear. You will hear the recording twice. There is an example (0) at the beginning.
instructionsHu: Egy rádiós vitaműsort hallasz arról, hogy kitiltsák-e a magánautókat egy város központjából. Az 1–8. kérdésnél válaszd ki a hallottak alapján legjobban illő választ (A, B, C vagy D). A felvételt kétszer hallod; a 0. a példa.

script.speaker: H
script.text: Good evening and welcome to The Big Question. Tonight we're asking whether Harbridge should ban private cars from its historic centre, as a number of European cities have already done. The city council is due to vote on the plan in March. With me are Tom Whitaker, a transport planner who has advised several cities on exactly this kind of scheme, and Linda Moreno, who runs a bakery on Market Street and chairs the local traders' association. Tom, let's start with you. Why should Harbridge do this?

script.speaker: T
script.text: Well, the simple answer is that the centre was never designed for cars in the first place. Some of those medieval streets are, what, six metres wide? We've squeezed traffic, parking and pedestrians into them, and nobody's really happy. Take the cars out and suddenly you've got space for people – for café tables, for markets, for kids to play safely. And air quality improves almost immediately.

script.speaker: L
script.text: Can I just come in there? Look, nobody's against cleaner air. Of course not. But it's easy to talk about café tables when you don't have to make a living in the centre. About forty per cent of my customers drive in from the villages. If they can't park nearby, they're not going to sit on a bus for half an hour to buy a loaf of bread. They'll just go to the big supermarket out on the ring road.

script.speaker: H
script.text: Tom, that's a fair point, isn't it?

script.speaker: T
script.text: It's a very common fear, and I don't dismiss it. But the research from other cities is remarkably consistent. Shopkeepers tend to overestimate how many of their customers arrive by car – often by as much as half. And people who come on foot or by bike may spend a bit less each time, but they come back more often. So over a month, they actually spend more.

script.speaker: L
script.text: With respect, Tom, Harbridge isn't Amsterdam. We don't have trams, and the last bus from most of the villages leaves at seven in the evening. You can't take away one option without offering people a real alternative first.

script.speaker: T
script.text: And I agree with you completely on that. The ban should only start once the new park-and-ride sites are open and the bus service runs later. Doing it the other way round would be a serious mistake – and I've seen it happen.

script.speaker: H
script.text: Where have you seen it happen?

script.speaker: T
script.text: I'd rather not name the city. But a few years ago I worked on a project where the centre was closed to cars almost overnight, because the politicians wanted a quick success before an election. The number of shoppers dropped by about a fifth in the first year, and several small shops closed. It took years to win back people's trust.

script.speaker: H
script.text: Linda, if those conditions were met – park-and-ride, later buses – could you support the plan?

script.speaker: L
script.text: Hmm. I'd be, well, cautiously open to it, let's put it that way. But what I really want is for traders to be involved from the very beginning, not consulted at the end when everything's already been decided. The last time the council consulted us, we got a leaflet through the door two weeks before the roadworks started. Very helpful.

script.speaker: H
script.text: And what about deliveries? Linda, how would you get your flour in?

script.speaker: L
script.text: Exactly! That's what I keep asking, and nobody gives me a straight answer.

script.speaker: T
script.text: Most schemes allow deliveries in the early morning, usually until ten. And residents, disabled drivers and emergency vehicles are normally exempt. A car-free centre isn't the same as a vehicle-free centre. That's probably the misunderstanding I come across most often.

script.speaker: H
script.text: We're almost out of time. Very briefly, what would you each say to a listener who's still undecided? Linda?

script.speaker: L
script.text: I'd say, ask yourself who the city centre is for. If it's only for people who can walk or cycle in, then we'll lose something. But if it's done carefully, for everyone, then, yes, I could live with it. I might even enjoy it.

script.speaker: T
script.text: And I'd say: think of your favourite square in any city you've visited on holiday. I'd be willing to bet there weren't many cars in it.

script.speaker: H
script.text: Tom Whitaker and Linda Moreno, thank you both.

example.prompt: Why has Linda Moreno been invited to the programme?

options.text: She works for the city council.
She represents local business owners.
She has advised other cities on transport.
She lives on Market Street.

example.explanation: B a helyes: Linda pékséget vezet, és ő a helyi kereskedők egyesületének elnöke („chairs the local traders' association”), tehát a helyi vállalkozókat képviseli.

wrongOptions.A: A városi tanács szavaz majd a tervről, de Linda nem ott dolgozik.
wrongOptions.D: A Market Streeten a pékségét vezeti; hogy ott lakik-e, nem derül ki.

items.prompt: What is Linda's main worry about the plan?

options.text: The air in the centre will become more polluted.
A new supermarket will open in the city centre.
The streets are too narrow for buses.
Customers who drive in from outside may shop elsewhere.

items.explanation: D a helyes: vásárlóinak kb. 40%-a autóval jön be a falvakból, és ha nem tudnak a közelben parkolni, nem buszoznak fél órát egy kenyérért, hanem a körgyűrű melletti nagy szupermarketbe mennek.
items.evidence: If they can't park nearby, they're not going to sit on a bus for half an hour to buy a loaf of bread.

wrongOptions.A: Azt mondja, senki sem ellenzi a tisztább levegőt – nem a szennyezés miatt aggódik.
wrongOptions.B: A szupermarket nem a központban nyílik, hanem már ott van kint a körgyűrűnél („out on the ring road”).
wrongOptions.C: A keskeny (kb. hatméteres) utcákat Tom említi, és nem a buszokkal kapcsolatban.

items.prompt: According to Tom, research shows that shopkeepers

options.text: believe that more of their customers drive than really do.
usually know exactly how their customers travel.
lose around half of their customers after a ban.
earn more from drivers than from cyclists over a month.

items.explanation: A a helyes: a boltosok túlbecsülik („overestimate”), hány vásárlójuk érkezik autóval – vagyis többen jönnek szerintük autóval, mint a valóságban.
items.evidence: Shopkeepers tend to overestimate how many of their customers arrive by car

wrongOptions.B: Éppen hogy rosszul becsülik meg, hogyan közlekednek a vásárlóik.
wrongOptions.C: Csapda: a „half” arra vonatkozik, hogy mennyivel becsülik túl az autósok arányát, nem a vásárlók elvesztésére.
wrongOptions.D: Fordítva: a gyalogosok és biciklisek egy hónap alatt összesen többet költenek, mert gyakrabban jönnek.

options.text: the ban should be introduced as quickly as possible.
Harbridge needs to build a tram network.
public transport must be improved before cars are banned.
buses from the villages should run all night.

items.explanation: C a helyes: Linda szerint nem lehet elvenni egy lehetőséget valódi alternatíva nélkül, Tom pedig teljesen egyetért: a tilalom csak akkor induljon, ha megnyíltak a P+R parkolók és a buszok később is járnak.
items.evidence: The ban should only start once the new park-and-ride sites are open and the bus service runs later.

wrongOptions.A: Tom szerint éppen hiba lenne a sietség („Doing it the other way round would be a serious mistake”).
wrongOptions.B: A villamost Linda csak azért említi, hogy Harbridge-ben nincs; építését senki sem javasolja.
wrongOptions.D: Csak arról van szó, hogy a buszok később járjanak („runs later”), nem egész éjjel.

items.prompt: What does Tom suggest about the project he worked on a few years ago?

options.text: It failed because there wasn't enough money.
It was introduced too quickly for political reasons.
Most of the shops in the centre had to close.
It was cancelled after the election.

items.explanation: B a helyes: a központot szinte egyik napról a másikra zárták le az autók elől, mert a politikusok gyors sikert akartak a választások előtt – vagyis politikai okból elsietett bevezetés volt.
items.evidence: because the politicians wanted a quick success before an election

wrongOptions.C: Nem a legtöbb, hanem „several small shops” zárt be, a vásárlók száma pedig kb. egyötödével csökkent.
wrongOptions.D: Nem mondja, hogy leállították volna; csak azt, hogy évekbe telt visszaszerezni az emberek bizalmát.

items.prompt: How does Linda feel about the plan if her conditions are met?

options.text: She would be prepared to consider it.
She would still strongly oppose it.
She would be enthusiastic about it.
She would only accept it if there were no roadworks.

items.explanation: A a helyes: azt mondja, „cautiously open to it” – óvatosan nyitott rá, vagyis hajlandó megfontolni, de nem lelkes.
items.evidence: I'd be, well, cautiously open to it, let's put it that way.

wrongOptions.B: Már nem ellenzi határozottan: óvatosan nyitott.
wrongOptions.C: A „cautiously” (óvatosan) éppen azt jelzi, hogy nem lelkes.
wrongOptions.D: Az útépítést csak a tanács rossz tájékoztatásának példájaként említi, nem feltételként.

items.prompt: When Linda says 'Very helpful', she is

options.text: thanking the council for keeping traders informed.
saying that the roadworks improved Market Street.
asking for more leaflets in the future.
criticising the way the council dealt with traders.

items.explanation: D a helyes: ironikusan mondja. A „konzultáció” csak egy szórólap volt két héttel az útépítés előtt, amikor már minden el volt döntve – a „Very helpful” tehát gúnyos kritika a tanács eljárásáról.
items.evidence: The last time the council consulted us, we got a leaflet through the door two weeks before the roadworks started. Very helpful.

wrongOptions.A: Nem köszönetet mond: ironikus, hiszen éppen azt kifogásolja, hogy a kereskedőket csak a végén tájékoztatták.
wrongOptions.B: Az útépítés eredményéről nem mond semmit.
wrongOptions.C: Nem több szórólapot akar, hanem azt, hogy a kereskedőket a kezdetektől vonják be.

items.prompt: Which misunderstanding does Tom want to clear up?

options.text: That residents will have to sell their cars.
That deliveries will only be possible at night.
That no vehicles at all will be allowed into the centre.
That emergency vehicles will need special permission.

items.explanation: C a helyes: az autómentes központ nem azonos a járműmentes központtal – reggel lehet szállítani, a lakók, a mozgássérült sofőrök és a mentők mentességet kapnak. Ez az a félreértés, amivel szerinte a leggyakrabban találkozik.
items.evidence: A car-free centre isn't the same as a vehicle-free centre.

wrongOptions.A: A lakók éppen mentességet kapnak; autóeladásról nincs szó.
wrongOptions.B: Az áruszállítás kora reggel, általában tízig lehetséges, nem éjjel.
wrongOptions.D: A mentő- és egyéb sürgősségi járművek „normally exempt”, vagyis nem kell külön engedély.

items.prompt: Why does Tom mention holidays at the end?

options.text: To argue that the plan will attract more tourists.
To get listeners to imagine how pleasant car-free spaces can be.
To point out that tourists cause most of the traffic.
To suggest that Harbridge is less attractive than other cities.

items.explanation: B a helyes: arra kéri a hallgatót, gondoljon a kedvenc terére egy városban, ahol nyaralt – és fogad, hogy ott nem volt sok autó. Így akarja elképzeltetni, milyen kellemes egy autómentes tér.
items.evidence: think of your favourite square in any city you've visited on holiday

wrongOptions.A: A turisták számának növekedéséről nem beszél.
wrongOptions.C: Nem mondja, hogy a forgalmat a turisták okozzák.
wrongOptions.D: Nem hasonlítja kedvezőtlenül Harbridge-et más városokhoz; csak egy élményt idéz fel.
